explanations.11: This uses parameter expansion to remove everything from the start of the string up to the first non-whitespace character, effectively trimming the left side without calling an external program.
explanations.12: Similarly, this trims the right side by removing everything from the last non-whitespace character to the end of the string.
explanations.19: The ${name^} syntax capitalizes just the first letter of the string (it's a bash 4+ feature for case transformation).
explanations.26: The ${2:-en} syntax means 'use the second argument if it was provided, otherwise use the default value en'.
explanations.31: The ${lang,,} converts the language to lowercase before checking it, so 'EN', 'En', and 'en' all match the same case branch.
explanations.52: This checks if the script was run directly versus being imported by another script; it only runs main() when someone executes the file, not when they source it for reuse.
